node.label: C. A. Bayly
node.date_label: Rulers, Townsmen and Bazaars (1983) · Empire and Information (1996) · The Birth of the Modern World (2004)
node.description: Historian of South Asia and empire whose global comparisons retained local and regional foundations. In Binu M. John’s interview Bayly explains modernity as interacting changes across several societies rather than a single Western essence. He also challenges accounts of an all-powerful colonial state by emphasizing Indian intermediaries and the uneven development of British rule. These positions coexist with his explicit refusal to identify only as a global historian.
